topics.label: Arrays & Dynamic Arrays
topics.desc: Contiguous indexed storage with O(1) random access; dynamic arrays (JS arrays, Python lists, vectors) amortize resizing, the default container you reach for in app code.

topics.label: Strings
topics.desc: Sequences of characters that are usually immutable, so repeated concatenation in loops is costly; full-stack devs hit this in parsing, slugs, templating, and input handling.

topics.label: Hash Maps & Sets
topics.desc: Key-value maps and unique-value sets giving average O(1) lookup via hashing; the workhorse behind JS objects, Maps, Sets, and Python dicts for caching, counting, and dedup.

topics.label: Stacks & Queues
topics.desc: LIFO stacks (call stack, undo, DFS) and FIFO queues and deques (task buffers, BFS, rate limiting), simple ordered structures backed by arrays or linked lists of nodes.

topics.label: Trees & BSTs
topics.desc: Hierarchical structures you meet as the DOM, file systems, and JSON, including binary search trees with O(log n) lookup and tries for fast prefix and autocomplete search.

topics.label: Heaps & Priority Queues
topics.desc: Partially ordered trees that pop the min or max in O(log n), powering priority queues, job schedulers, top-K results, and Dijkstra-style shortest-path algorithms.

topics.label: Graphs
topics.desc: Nodes joined by edges modeling social networks, dependencies, and routing, stored as adjacency lists or matrices and explored with BFS or DFS traversal.

topics.label: Choosing The Structure
topics.desc: Picking a container by the operations you do most — lookup, ordering, dedup, or FIFO — which often matters more in real app code than any clever algorithm.

topics.label: Binary & Linear Search
topics.desc: Linear scan in O(n) for small or unsorted data versus binary search halving a sorted range in O(log n), the classic technique behind sorted lookups and answer-space search.

topics.label: Sorting Algorithms
topics.desc: Ordering data with quicksort, mergesort, and heapsort, plus the language's built-in sort and comparators; they run in O(n log n) and may or may not be stable.

topics.label: Recursion
topics.desc: Solving a problem by calling itself on smaller inputs with a base case, natural for trees and divide-and-conquer but mindful of stack depth and repeated work.

topics.label: BFS & DFS
topics.desc: Breadth-first search level by level with a queue for shortest paths, versus depth-first search via recursion or a stack for tree walks, cycle detection, and topological sort.

topics.label: Two Pointers & Window
topics.desc: Walking two indices through a sorted array or maintaining a moving sub-range over a string, turning many brute-force O(n²) scans into a single linear pass.

topics.label: Hashing For Lookup
topics.desc: Trading memory for speed by storing seen values in a hash map or set to replace nested O(n²) scans with O(n) single passes, the most common interview trick.

topics.label: Greedy Algorithms
topics.desc: Building a solution by always taking the locally best choice, which is fast and works for problems like interval scheduling but can miss the global optimum.

topics.label: Dynamic Programming
topics.desc: Solving overlapping subproblems once and caching results via memoization or tabulation, the go-to for counting, optimization, and sequence-matching problems.

topics.label: Big-O Notation
topics.desc: Describing how an algorithm's cost grows with input size, the shared vocabulary for reasoning about scalability without benchmarking every implementation.

topics.label: Time Vs Space
topics.desc: The recurring tradeoff between doing fewer operations and using more memory, like caching results or building an index to cut runtime at the cost of storage.

topics.label: Complexity Classes
topics.desc: The everyday ladder from O(1) to O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²), and O(2ⁿ) that tells you at a glance whether code will survive larger inputs.

topics.label: Amortized Analysis
topics.desc: Averaging cost over a sequence of operations so an occasional expensive step, like a dynamic array resize, still counts as cheap per operation overall.

topics.label: Cost Of Operations
topics.desc: Knowing the real cost of common moves — array shift, hash lookup, sort, nested loop — so you can spot the expensive line in a function just by reading it.

topics.label: Premature Optimization
topics.desc: Resisting micro-tuning before profiling, since clarity usually wins and most real slowdowns come from a wrong data structure or an N+1 query, not slow loops.

topics.label: TCP/IP Model
topics.desc: The layered stack — link, internet (IP), transport (TCP/UDP), application (HTTP) — that frames how your app's bytes actually travel across a network.

topics.label: Ports & Sockets
topics.desc: The IP-plus-port endpoint your server binds and a client connects to; the model behind listening on a port, EADDRINUSE errors, and raw socket programming.

topics.label: HTTP Request Lifecycle
topics.desc: What happens between a fetch and a response — DNS, connect, send headers and body, receive status and body, close or reuse — the path every API call follows.

topics.label: Latency Vs Bandwidth
topics.desc: Latency is the delay per round trip and bandwidth is throughput; chatty apps suffer from latency, big payloads from bandwidth, and the fix differs for each.

topics.label: Client-Server Round Trips
topics.desc: Each request-response is a round trip whose latency stacks up, so batching, caching, and connection reuse cut the round trips that dominate perceived speed.

topics.label: TLS Handshake
topics.desc: The extra encrypted round trips that set up an HTTPS connection, why the first secure request costs more, and how keep-alive and TLS 1.3 reduce that overhead.

topics.label: Processes Vs Threads
topics.desc: Processes are isolated with their own memory; threads share memory within one process, which is cheaper but exposes you to data races needing synchronization.

topics.label: Concurrency Vs Parallelism
topics.desc: Concurrency is juggling many tasks by interleaving them; parallelism is truly running them at once on multiple cores — overlapping ideas that are not the same thing.

topics.label: Event Loop
topics.desc: The single-threaded loop in JavaScript and Node that runs tasks and microtasks, so blocking it with heavy synchronous work freezes the whole application.

topics.label: Async/Await & Promises
topics.desc: Promises represent future values and async/await makes asynchronous I/O read like sequential code, the default way full-stack devs handle network and disk waits.

topics.label: Callbacks
topics.desc: Passing a function to run when an async operation finishes, the original Node pattern whose nesting (callback hell) motivated promises and async/await.

topics.label: Race Conditions & Deadlocks
topics.desc: Timing-dependent bugs where concurrent operations clash, like two requests updating one record, and deadlocks where each task waits forever on a resource the other holds.

topics.label: Workers & Web Workers
topics.desc: Offloading CPU-heavy work to separate threads — web workers in the browser, worker threads in Node — to keep the main event loop responsive.

topics.label: Decomposing Problems
topics.desc: Breaking a vague task into smaller, testable pieces with clear inputs and outputs, the first move that makes both features and interview questions tractable.

topics.label: Common Coding Patterns
topics.desc: A reusable toolkit — two pointers, sliding window, hashing, BFS/DFS, dynamic programming — that recurs across problems so you recognize the shape, not memorize answers.

topics.label: Debugging Strategy
topics.desc: Reproducing reliably, forming a hypothesis, and bisecting to isolate the cause instead of changing code at random, the everyday skill that dwarfs raw algorithm chops.

topics.label: Reading Tradeoffs
topics.desc: Estimating an approach's time and space cost from the input size up front so you choose a viable design before writing it, not after it times out.

topics.label: Interview Patterns
topics.desc: Mapping a problem to a known LeetCode-style pattern and the data structure it implies, the practical way to prepare for technical interviews over grinding random questions.

topics.label: Structure Over Cleverness
topics.desc: Reaching for the fitting data structure usually beats clever tricks, turning a tangled nested loop into a clear, fast, and maintainable hash-map lookup.

topics.label: Brute Force First
topics.desc: Getting a correct naive solution working first, then improving its complexity, so you always have something that runs and a baseline to measure against.
